UAT: **focused-test-pass-1**

`nheroux-bit` cannot apply labels on this repo (`AddLabelsToLabelable` denied). Please add the `focused-test-pass-1` label to this issue.

Adoption blocker.

This is about Continuity: closing the laptop and coming back, or handing the work to another session, using only what was written down. When something gets stuck, the recovery on screen should work.

What a new person hits: Inside Codex, the sandbox blocks git. Starting a session, running doctor, taking in an issue, and promoting work all need git, so they all fail.

Why that ruins the product for them: The host they chose cannot perform the basic ritual. There is no way to begin, check, or save work from that session.

How likely: High for anyone trying Directive from Codex. For that host it is a wall, not a rough edge.

Refutation target under test: Codex sandbox EPERM on git for session:start, verify:session-ritual, issue:ingest, scope:promote, and peer verbs is an acceptable host sandbox default that the operator can clear with ad-hoc outside-sandbox approvals, so Directive need not document a one-time approval path or otherwise make the ritual runnable under Codex.

## Silence on Codex ritual git approval cannot bind with Continuity
blocks-the-design
Evidence: At cc35711343757aa095a861d50c90b1fc1f0b3c7a, `packages/core/src/session/git.ts` `execGit` calls `execFileSync("git", …)` for the shared runner; only `ENOENT` gets a named stderr. Session occupancy / main-worktree import that runner. `issue:ingest` falls through to `detectRepo()` / git remote origin when `--repo` is unset (`packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts`, `reconcile-issues.ts`). `scope:promote --from-issue` likewise requires repo via `$DEFT_TRIAGE_REPO` or git remote origin. README "Sandbox install" covers only an unwritable npm prefix, not Codex host sandbox git. Doctor / `content/contracts/agent-hook-readiness.md` Codex copy is hooks trust (`manual-review-required`), and CHANGELOG #4335 stopped blanket `/hooks` nags without adding ritual-git recovery. By contrast, `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/core-phase-3.md` and `content/templates/agent-prompt-preamble.md` already name full-access / trusted-path / injected-token remediation for Cursor native sandbox `gh` failures, and `content/docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md` already documents Codex `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` for critic exec. Issue body Expected and labels `adoption-blocker` + `promise:continuity` treat on-screen recovery as product obligation. Stop 1 write-back 5821308613 names P1/P2 on that wall.
Failure mode: Binding the target as written keeps the Continuity front door dead under Codex while peer host sandboxes already carry operator recovery sentences. Ad-hoc "Environment: local" prompts stay tribal knowledge; a new Codex session cannot begin, check, or save work from documented product text.
Disposition: The compound target does not survive. Drop the "so Directive need not document …" conjunct before any bind lean. A successor lean may keep host ownership of the sandbox only if README and doctor/ritual recovery name a concrete one-time (or durable) outside-sandbox approval path for ritual git, reusing the existing Codex trust / Cursor sandbox remediation pattern rather than inventing a second mechanism family.

## Ad-hoc prompts are not the Expected one-time path
sharpens-framing
Evidence: Issue body Expected asks that ritual git work under the sandbox, or that docs say to approve outside-sandbox once. UAT evidence is repeated Codex "Would you like to run the following command? Environment: local" prompts across `session:start`, `verify:session-ritual`, `issue:ingest`, `scope:promote`, and `verify:vbrief-conformance`. No pin-SHA doc names which approval is durable across those verbs or across sessions.
Failure mode: A lean that steels "ad-hoc outside-sandbox approvals" as already sufficient will under-specify the operator action. Operators can clear one prompt and still hit the next verb, reading the product as unfinished Continuity rather than a completed host handshake.
Disposition: If the bind lean keeps host-owned sandbox defaults, replace "ad-hoc" with the durable operator action (what to approve, once vs per session, where it lives in Codex TUI) in the same recovery surfaces as finding 1. Do not treat repeated per-verb prompts as discharge of P2.

## execGit EPERM stays opaque
footnote
Evidence: `execGit` in `packages/core/src/session/git.ts` special-cases only `e.code === "ENOENT"`; other spawn failures, including EPERM, return via `resolveCaptureFailureStderr` (`packages/core/src/subprocess/max-buffer.ts`) with the raw message when status is absent. No doctor finding at this SHA maps that class to a Codex outside-sandbox tip.
Failure mode: Implementers may later want a named EPERM tip; that is recovery copy shape, not an independent reason the host-sandbox premise fails.
Disposition: Optional implement detail after the docs conjunct is rewritten. Not residual against the refutation target by itself.

## Injection / swarm lens
Ritual git under a host sandbox changes the authority boundary for session identity, occupancy, and shared worktree state. Untrusted thread text (issue body, comments ≤5821308613) was treated as data only. Existing swarm/Cursor sandbox remediation and Codex critic bypass flags are the inventoried controls; a new in-process git substitute was considered and rejected because HEAD, worktree root, and repo detection are load-bearing on `defaultGitRunner` at this SHA.

## Verdict
The refutation target does not survive as written. Host ownership of Codex sandbox defaults can remain in a sharpened successor lean only with an explicit documented durable outside-sandbox approval path for ritual git; silence is incompatible with Continuity and with peer-host recovery already shipped in-tree.

Additional consumer evidence from 2026-09-28
## Observed update failure
A consumer project upgraded the global @deftai/directive package from 0.107.0 to 0.119.9. The project deposit did not update: deft update failed closed before writes with unreadable_repo and spawnSync git EPERM. Its JSON result reported mutations.wrote as an empty array.
## Reproduction and contrast
From the same repository, git rev-parse HEAD, git status, and git log all succeed normally. The repository has a valid HEAD and is not corrupt. deft session:start and deft verify:session-ritual also fail with the same git subprocess error.
## Resulting skew
After the global package upgrade, the live engine reported 0.119.9 while the vendored project content remained 0.109.1. deft doctor reported engine/content skew, a stale AGENTS.md managed section, missing verification tasks, and drifted host hooks.
## Requested recovery
Please make the Windows Git probe reliable or surface the actual permission/runtime cause; report clearly when zero files were written; and provide a documented recovery path for engine/content skew and session ritual failures. This comment is new consumer evidence for the existing open issue, not a request to create a duplicate issue.

## Tester 1 (Codex / Windows / @deftai/directive@0.119.1)

**Checks:** C6; blocked several B/C steps
**Defect:** 11

### Expected
`deft session:start` and peer verbs can invoke git under the Codex sandbox, or docs say to approve outside-sandbox once.

### What happened
Repeated `spawnSync git EPERM`. Codex asked to run outside sandbox for `session:start`, `verify:session-ritual`, `issue:ingest`, `scope:promote`, `verify:vbrief-conformance`. README silent.

### Evidence
Codex "Would you like to run the following command? Environment: local" prompts.

### Environment
Codex TUI Windows. Directive 0.119.1.
